item.title: Narita Unagi Guide: Best Eel Restaurants & Access
item.description: The temple town of Narita is one of the best places near Tokyo to feast on unagi (freshwater eel) — a tradition stretching back centuries to feed pilgrims visiting Narita-san. Along the atmospheric Omotesando approach to the temple, dozens of long-established eel restaurants fillet, skewer and grill eel fresh to order, often in full view of the street, then glaze it in sweet-savoury tare sauce over rice as unadon or unaju.

item.title: Chiba Food Guide: Unagi, Sashimi, Peanuts & Pacific Seafood
item.description: Chiba Prefecture sits on the Pacific and Tokyo Bay, and its food culture reflects that position directly. The prefecture produces over 80 percent of Japan’s peanuts, operates Japan’s largest fishing port at Choshi, and hosts one of the oldest unagi-dining traditions in the country along the approach road to Naritasan Temple. For overseas visitors willing to venture beyond Narita Airport’s restaurants and the Disney Resort food courts, Chiba offers some of the most distinctive and affordable culinary experiences in the entire Kanto region.

item.title: Saitama Food Guide: Sweet Potato, Musashino Udon & Chichibu Whisky
item.description: Saitama does not have the culinary reputation of Osaka or Kyoto, but for visitors who dig beneath the surface, it offers some remarkably distinctive food experiences — the kind that cannot be replicated anywhere else in Japan. Kawagoe’s sweet potato culture stretches back three centuries. Musashino udon, thick and chewy and served in pork-bone broth, represents one of the Kanto region’s most underappreciated regional noodle traditions. And in the mountains of Chichibu, a small distillery has produced what many whisky critics regard as the finest Japanese single malt outside the major established brands.
